hypotheses.claim: Prefixing open semantic relation names with a one-character sigil can eliminate the observed identifier/operator lexical ambiguity while preserving relation identity and requiring no ClayCode semantic redesign.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A declared bare-infix relation design with contextual lexing/resolution provides equal or better stability and lower reader/repair cost without ambiguity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full admitted-corpus parser/roundtrip tests show sigil normalization changes meaning, creates new ambiguity, raises repair/token cost materially, or performs worse than declared bare-infix syntax.

hypotheses.claim: Open relation names belong in the typed symbol/resolution layer after lexical disambiguation; parser acceptance must not implicitly mint semantics for unknown relation names.
hypotheses.falsifier: A simpler grammar-only closed relation set covers the frozen/general-purpose language without extensibility loss, or typed relation resolution adds avoidable ambiguity/cost without benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Allowing arbitrary identifier-as-infix syntax is superior to strict lexical relation marking.
hypotheses.falsifier: A declared contextual-infix implementation parses the complete corpus with stable AST, precise typo diagnostics, equal semantic-hash preservation and lower measured reader/token/repair cost than the sigil candidate.

negative_results.claim: The current path of bare open relation words remains unsafe to freeze without an explicit lexical/resolution policy; prior E2B replication already exposed an identifier-vs-relation ambiguity, while the sigil proxy removes it at the tested scope.
